\section{A Working Demonstration: Kazakhstan's Commercial Research Landscape}
\label{sec:demo}

To show that the National Innovation Operating System is a functioning instrument
rather than a proposal, we ran its measurement layer over Kazakhstan's research
base directly through the \texttt{scientifiq.ai} API. Every Kazakhstan-affiliated
publication was scored for commercial, scientific, and social potential; the
results below---a national map, an institutional ranking, a field-level heatmap,
and a sample deep-technology portfolio---were generated automatically and are
continuously refreshable. They correspond to Work Packages~1 and~2.

\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}
  % country extent (schematic)
  \draw[rounded corners=6pt, draw=gray!40, fill=gray!6] (-0.4,-0.4) rectangle (13.4,6.8);

  \fill[teal!55,opacity=0.75] (9.57,1.24) circle (0.74);

\caption{Geography of high-commercial-potential research. Bubble area is proportional to the number of Kazakhstan-affiliated publications with commercial potential $\geq 0.6$ at each city's institutions. Output is concentrated in Astana and Almaty, with Shymkent emerging---a concentration that is itself a finding for regional innovation policy.}
\label{fig:kz-map}
\end{figure}

Figure~\ref{fig:kz-map} locates the nation's commercially promising science.
Table~\ref{tab:kz-rank} ranks institutions by the volume of that science, and
Table~\ref{tab:kz-heatmap} shows \emph{where} each institution's commercial
strength lies by field. Together they give a ministry an evidence base for
concentrating support: which institutions to back, and in which domains.
